distractors: PAUT does not use film.
There is no radiation dose.
They do not cool hardware.
content.explanation: Focal laws apply element delays to steer and focus the beam to the required angles and depths.

content.stem: A sectorial (S) scan sweeps the beam through:
options: A single fixed angle held through the scan
The film emulsion loaded in the cassette
A range of angles from a fixed element group
The coating layer on the outside of the pipe
distractors: A fixed angle is not a sweep.
No film is involved.
Coating is not scanned.
content.explanation: An S-scan sweeps a range of angles, imaging a cross-section of the weld.

content.stem: A PAUT setup is calibrated on a reference standard to set:
options: The film density read across the joint
Sensitivity and range across the focal laws
The developer time used in processing
The activity of the source loaded for it itself
distractors: Density is radiographic.
Developer is radiographic.
No source is used.
content.explanation: Calibration on a reference block sets sensitivity and range across the angles used.

content.stem: Encoded scanning is used so that each data point is:
options: Printed out to a radiographic film
Averaged away to smooth the displayed trace
Tied to a position on the weld for the map
Discarded once the operator has viewed it
distractors: PAUT is not printed to film.
Data is retained, not averaged away.
Data is recorded, not discarded.
content.explanation: An encoder links data to circumferential position, producing a recordable map.

content.stem: Coupling monitoring during a PAUT scan guards against:
options: Film fog appearing during the processing
Loss of sound transfer leaving data gaps
Overexposure of the film on the shot
Ovality of the pipe measured at the joint
distractors: Film fog is radiographic.
Overexposure is radiographic.
Ovality is unrelated.
content.explanation: Coupling loss creates data gaps, so it is monitored and re-scanned.

content.stem: Acceptance criteria are applied to PAUT data by the:
options: The Level II analyst or the company
The Level I operator running the instrument
The probe maker that built the array
The couplant supplier providing the gel
distractors: Level I records, not dispositions.
Makers do not interpret.
Suppliers do not interpret.
content.explanation: Interpretation to acceptance is a Level II/company function.

content.stem: Under the workmanship route, PAUT indications are limited mainly by:
options: Color shown on the analyst's display itself
The size of the stored data file
The speed the scanner travelled at
Length measured along the line of the weld
distractors: Color is not measured.
File size is irrelevant.
Speed is a setup detail.
content.explanation: The workmanship route relies on indication length; height is an ECA input.

content.stem: A crack-like planar reflector in PAUT data is:
options: Ignored entirely whenever it measures short itself
Acceptable as long as it sits off the root
Treated as critical and rejectable in the weld
Beyond what PAUT is actually able to detect
distractors: Length does not make it acceptable.
Location does not make it acceptable.
PAUT detects planar flaws well.
content.explanation: Planar crack-like flaws are critical and rejectable.

content.stem: Beam angles are chosen so the scan covers:
options: The finished weld cap surface only
The root bead region of the joint only
The pipe body away from the welded joint itself
The full weld volume and the fusion faces
distractors: Cap-only is incomplete.
Root-only is incomplete.
The body is not the target.
content.explanation: Angle sets are arranged to cover the weld volume and fusion faces.

content.stem: Compared with single-angle UT, PAUT adds:
options: Lower sensitivity than a single-angle probe itself
A requirement to also shoot a radiograph
No calibration before the scan begins
Multiple steered angles and an imaged data set
distractors: PAUT is not designed to be less sensitive.
No film is used.
Calibration is still required.
content.explanation: PAUT steers many angles and produces imaging, improving coverage and interpretation.

content.stem: PAUT calibration validity is affected by a change in:
options: Part or wedge temperature during the scan
The ambient light level at the work site itself
The brand of film loaded for the joint
The color of paint applied to the pipe
distractors: Light does not change velocity.
No film is used.
Color is irrelevant.
content.explanation: Temperature shifts velocity and wedge behavior, affecting calibration.

content.stem: A PAUT-rejected section after repair is:
options: Re-scanned to the same method and criteria
Accepted on the strength of the repair note
Judged the second time by relaxed limits
Exempt from re-test once it is repaired
distractors: A note is not re-inspection.
Limits do not relax.
Re-scan is required.
content.explanation: The repair is re-examined to the same method and acceptance basis.

content.stem: Final acceptance of a PAUT-examined weld rests with the:
options: The company, applying the acceptance criteria
The Level I operator running the scan
The software vendor for the analysis tool itself
The pipe mill that supplied the joint
distractors: Level I does not disposition.
Vendors do not disposition.
The mill supplies pipe only.
content.explanation: The company dispositions the weld using the criteria and the recorded data.

content.stem: PAUT for API 1104 compliance is performed by personnel who are:
options: Members of the welding crew on the spread
Chosen by lottery among the available hands itself
Qualified and certified for the PAUT technique
Approved by the coating crew on the line
distractors: Welders are not the NDT authority.
Qualification is not by chance.
Coaters do not certify PAUT.
content.explanation: Examinations are performed by qualified, certified PAUT personnel.

content.stem: PAUT records submitted for acceptance should include:
options: Just a simple pass or fail stamp on the weld on the joint
The film density read through the weld
The radiographic IQI placed by the joint
Indication position and length, plus height as required
distractors: A bare stamp is not a record.
Density is radiographic.
IQIs are radiographic.
content.explanation: The report captures indication position and size, with height where ECA applies.
